v02.en: This is a real Nerdearla talk, captioned and translated live, by an open source system anyone can run.

v03.en: At a conference, every room is a different talk, and not everyone speaks the speaker's language.

v04.en: Subtítulos en vivo listens to each room, transcribes it in real time, and translates it. English to Spanish, Spanish to English, and more.

v05.en: Each room gets its own process. The audio streams to Gemini Live for transcription, the text is translated in short batches, and a central server sends the captions to every screen.

v06.en: The audience scans a QR code, and picks a room and a language.

v07.en: The same captions drive the room's projector, a transparent overlay for the livestream, and an operator panel that tracks every room.

v08.en: It scales on three axes: rooms against the API, viewers per room, and a replay mode that runs the whole system without an API key.

v09.en: Deployment is one docker compose command.

v10.en: In a run of almost ten minutes, with two real rooms at once, no stretch of speech went uncaptioned, and the median perceived delay stayed under half a second.

v11.en: Subtítulos en vivo. Open source, and built for any conference.
